instruction: Make the mouse cursor bigger so it's easier to spot on screen.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.click({SCREEN_WIDTH_HALF}, {SCREEN_HEIGHT_HALF}); time.sleep(0.5);

result.command: CURSOR_SIZE=$(timeout 10 gsettings get org.gnome.desktop.interface cursor-size 2>/dev/null); if [ -n "$CURSOR_SIZE" ] && [ "$CURSOR_SIZE" -gt 24 ] 2>/dev/null; then echo "Cursor size enlarged to $CURSOR_SIZE"; else echo "Cursor size is default or unchanged ($CURSOR_SIZE)"; fi

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent successfully opened GNOME Settings via system menu, navigated to Accessibility section, and toggled Large Text ON in 7 turns.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can open system menu, navigate GNOME Settings sidebar, find Accessibility section, toggle switches on/off
metadata.task_rationale: Tests accessibility settings interaction with a different control type (cursor size selector instead of toggle), visible in the same Accessibility panel the model navigated to
metadata.explanation: Task requires increasing the cursor size via Settings > Accessibility > Cursor Size. Evaluator checks if cursor-size gsetting is larger than the default of 24.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly uses gsettings to read org.gnome.desktop.interface cursor-size, which is the standard GNOME way to check cursor size
Default GNOME cursor size is 24; checking > 24 correctly verifies the cursor was made bigger
Shell command handles edge cases with timeout and stderr redirection, producing clear output strings
Metric check_include_exclude correctly receives rules dict directly (type=rule) and checks include/exclude patterns that match the command output strings
Single instruction requirement (make cursor bigger) is fully covered by the evaluator
No postconfig needed since gsettings persists state and does not depend on UI dialogs being open
